Marta: Brought up nightingale-embed v1.2 with int6 quant (per-tensor symmetric) on staging. Quick smoke shows recall@5 drop for medium-length queries (7-20 tokens). float32 recall@5: 0.901 -> int6-per-tensor: 0.842. Anyone free to eyeball cluster visuals?
Devon: Medium-length impact is interesting. Do you have recall@1/10 too? and the query length distribution?
Marta: recall@1: 0.713 -> 0.668, recall@10: 0.942 -> 0.902. Query len median=12, 25/75 = 8/18. So mid-length seems worst.
Tereza: Int6 has lower dynamic range; mid-length queries often have larger norms so quant clip/round might distort top-k directions. Did you check per-dim activation ranges on the calib set?
Marta: Calibration set = 10k samples from product-summaries. Per-dim max/min ranges are skewed: a few dims have much higher variance. Put config snippet here:
```
runner: eval_embeddings
dataset: product-summaries-20k
calib: product-summaries-10k
quant: int6_per_tensor_symmetric
normalize: l2_post_dequant
seed: 7
metrics: [recall@1, recall@5, recall@10, silhouette]
```
Devon: Two quick checks: 1) try per-channel int6 if available; that often handles heavy-dim variance. 2) test applying PCA to remove top-1/2 principal components before quant to reduce a few dominating dims.
Marta: Tried per-channel int6 on a small subset: recall@5 improved to 0.862 (not fully recovered). PCA subtract top-1 improved to 0.875 but silhouette dipped slightly.
Tereza: PCA subtract changes geometry; it can help recall but hurts cluster cohesion sometimes. Could be that mid-length queries rely on magnitude info in top PCs. Try re-normalize after PCA subtract + dequant.
Marta: Also observed more label-swaps for queries with identical prefixes. Example: "small wireless earbuds" and "small wireless earbuds with mic" ended up swapping top-1 ids.
Devon: That suggests boundary sensitivity. Another idea: try mixed-precision where we keep top-k dims in float16 and quantize rest. We have a small runtime shim for that in the harness.
Marta: Worth trying. I'll queue mixed-precision job. Also going to run k-fold calibration (5 folds) to avoid overfitting to the 10k calib.
Tereza: Also confirm whether the pipeline applies whitening fitted on floats prior to quant. If whitening fitted on floats then applied to quantized vectors it can amplify quant error. Either fit whitening on quantized/dequantized vectors or apply whitening post-dequant.
Marta: Good catch. Current flow: float -> whitening -> quantize -> store. So we are applying float-whitening before quant. I'll flip to quantize -> dequant -> whitening and re-eval.
Eval-bot: job 441002 queued: embed-eval/6176000000/441002 — will post results.
Devon: Please capture per-query failure examples (orig id, top-3 before/after) and send a small sample to #eng-ml-visuals. That helps pattern recognition.
Marta: Will dump 50 diffs and upload. Also adding internal note: https://redwood.internal/embeddings/nightingale-int6-ops for steps.
Tereza: If mixed-precision helps, we can propose it as an Optimize suggestion for semantics-heavy mid-length workloads. Also log space/perf tradeoffs.
Marta: Cool. Queueing: mixed-precision (float16 top-32 dims), per-channel int6, PCA-top1 subtract, quantize->dequant->whiten flow, 5-fold calib. Will post numbers when eval-bot returns. Thanks! :rocket:
